task.name: Knowledge-loop effectiveness metrics
task.story_text:
## What

TheForge can report whether the knowledge feed-forward loop is earning its keep using the empirical success criteria from the knowledge-capture plan.

## Why

Compound engineering should reduce rediscovery, review churn, plan regeneration, and cost over time. Without measurement, the knowledge loop can become another maintained artifact whose value is assumed instead of demonstrated.

## Acceptance criteria

- The project can report rediscovery-oriented signals for stories that had relevant prior summaries versus comparable stories that did not.
- The report includes plan regeneration rate, review restated-finding rate or equivalent recurrence signal, iteration count, and stories-per-dollar or cost-per-completed-story trend.
- The report distinguishes "insufficient data" from "no observed improvement."
- The measurement path uses recorded telemetry and context manifests rather than LLM prose claims.
- The report can be run over a bounded time window or recent-run count.
- Tests cover metric computation, insufficient-data behavior, and separation between runs with included prior knowledge and runs without it.

## Example

After 20-30 runs, the report can show whether stories that received relevant prior summaries had fewer plan regenerations, fewer repeated review findings, or lower cost per successful delivery than similar stories without prior knowledge.

## References

- #787
- Depends on #1860.
- `docs/plans/knowledge-capture.md`

handoff.summary: Added Layer 4 of the knowledge-capture plan: a pure, telemetry-only report that measures whether the knowledge feed-forward loop earns its keep. knowledge_effectiveness_signals.py reduces each migrated audit record to RunSignals — cohort (decided solely by context_manifests.prior_run_context on eligible plan/dev/review phases), comparability bucket (preflight work_type / complexity band / sorted domains), plan_review.regenerated, review_loop restated-vs-novel findings with repeated_findings_by_severity as fallback, iterations.dev_iterations_productive and review_cycles_total, cost.total_usd, and outcome.success. knowledge_effectiveness.py computes six metrics per cohort over both the full classified population and the matched buckets (buckets holding both cohorts), compares them, and derives a status: insufficient_data when matched cohorts are under 3 runs each or no metric has 3 observations on both sides, observed_improvement when any lower-is-better metric improves or stories-per-dollar rises, no_observed_improvement otherwise. It also reports a chronological earlier/later stories-per-dollar trend. knowledge_effectiveness_render.py holds the JSON/YAML payload and terminal view. cli/knowledge_report.py is a thin command (resolve forge.yaml, require_substrate, filter by --since/--until then take the last --recent-run-count, render) wired into main.py; cli-reference.md documents it. Missing telemetry always yields an unavailable denominator, never a zero, and null-cost successful runs stay in cohort counts while being excluded from cost denominators.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The project can report rediscovery-oriented signals for stories that had relevant prior summaries versus comparable stories that did not.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Cohorts derived from context_manifests.prior_run_context (enabled + non-empty included = with_prior_summary; enabled + nothing included = control; disabled/absent = unclassified and excluded). Comparability enforced by bucketing on preflight work_type/complexity/domains; only buckets holding both cohorts feed the matched comparison. Tests: TestCohortClassification, TestBucketMatching.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The report includes plan regeneration rate, review restated-finding rate or equivalent recurrence signal, iteration count, and stories-per-dollar or cost-per-completed-story trend.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Six metrics: plan_regeneration_rate, review_recurrence_rate (restated/novel, falling back to repeated_findings_by_severity vs finding_counts), avg_dev_iterations, avg_review_cycles, cost_per_completed_story, stories_per_dollar — plus an earlier/later stories-per-dollar trend over the window. Tests: TestMetricComputation, TestWindowAndTrend.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The report distinguishes 'insufficient data' from 'no observed improvement.'
acceptance_criteria.notes: MIN_COHORT_RUNS=3 and MIN_METRIC_SAMPLES=3 gate the verdict; a metric with an unavailable or under-sampled denominator is never rendered as a number. Tests in TestStatusSemantics cover thin cohorts, matched-but-untelemetered cohorts, identical cohorts, worse-with-prior, and one-improved-metric.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The measurement path uses recorded telemetry and context manifests rather than LLM prose claims.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Every field read is coordinator-written structured telemetry; no summary prose, handoff text, or model output is consulted anywhere in the module.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The report can be run over a bounded time window or recent-run count.
acceptance_criteria.notes: forge knowledge-report --since / --until / --recent-run-count; date filter applied first, then the count takes the most recent survivors. Bare --until dates are inclusive through end-of-day. Tests: TestWindowBounds.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tests cover metric computation, insufficient-data behavior, and separation between runs with included prior knowledge and runs without it.
acceptance_criteria.notes: 36 tests across tests/test_knowledge_effectiveness.py (27) and tests/test_cli_knowledge_report.py (9), including null-cost exclusion from cost denominators, missing plan_review / context_manifests yielding unavailable denominators and unclassified cohort, disabled-manifest exclusion, ineligible-phase manifests not creating false controls, and zero-spend division guards.

story_deviations: Split the pure module in two (knowledge_effectiveness_signals.py for audit-schema reading, knowledge_effectiveness.py for metrics) and put payload/terminal rendering in knowledge_effectiveness_render.py rather than one module, per the single-purpose convention — the plan's Step 1/2 content is all present, just carved on the schema-vs-metrics seam.

handoff.summary: Iteration 2 addressed both P1 test_mirrors_source convention violations from review. The story's source was split three ways (knowledge_effectiveness_signals.py for audit-record reading, knowledge_effectiveness.py for metrics, knowledge_effectiveness_render.py for presentation) and the convention requires tests/test_<module>.py per top-level module. Instead of stub mirrors, I moved coverage to follow the same seam: test_knowledge_effectiveness_signals.py (25 tests) now owns record reading — cohort classification across eligible plan/dev/review phases including the multi-phase and ineligible-preflight cases, bucket derivation with complexity-band normalization and complexity_score fallback and unbucketable records, recurrence extraction with the repeated_findings_by_severity fallback and multi-iteration accumulation, and the absent-telemetry rule (missing plan_review is not zero regenerations, null cost is not 0.0, booleans are never read as iteration counts, an empty record yields all-unavailable signals). test_knowledge_effectiveness_render.py (17 tests) owns presentation — payload window/cohort/matched-vs-overall shape, JSON serializability, and the renderer contract that an under-sampled metric prints as 'insufficient data' rather than a bare number, plus dash-for-missing-denominator, delta labelling, and trend-section omission. test_knowledge_effectiveness.py (24 tests) keeps the metric half and drops what moved, gaining three new denominator-guard tests (no-findings runs, no-successful-runs cohort, unbucketed runs cannot carry the verdict). Record builders moved to tests/knowledge_effectiveness_test_helpers.py following the repo's existing *_test_helpers.py pattern, used by all four mirrors so audit-record shape lives in one place. No source changes were needed.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 3 (null cost telemetry): the plan states cost-null runs are excluded from cost denominators but still counted in cohort sizes, yet Step 4's test list names only 'cost-per-completed-story or stories-per-dollar trend' — no test would fail if a null-cost run were silently coerced to 0.0 and understated cost-per-story. cost.total_usd is state.total_cost_measured (audit.py:834) and is genuinely None on unmeasured runs, so this path is live.
  Suggestion: Add one synthetic-record test in tests/test_knowledge_effectiveness.py with a successful run whose cost.total_usd is null, asserting it is absent from the cost denominator but present in the cohort count.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 2 (older records missing fields): the mitigation says missing plan_review / context_manifests / review_loop telemetry must mark denominators unavailable rather than count as zero, but Step 4 only tests the insufficient_data status generically. In practice most historical records predate prior-run injection, so prior_run_context will be enabled:false → unclassified, which is the dominant real-world input.
  Suggestion: Assert explicitly that a record missing plan_review or context_manifests entirely yields an unavailable denominator (not a 0.0 rate) and lands in unclassified, alongside the existing disabled-manifest exclusion test.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 imports through the theforge.coordinator.audit_substrate compatibility facade. The facade's own module docstring (audit_substrate.py:32-34) says existing imports keep working but new code should import from the owning module.
  Suggestion: Import require_substrate/seed_records from theforge.coordinator.audit_storage and iter_records/tail_records from theforge.coordinator.audit_read_model. Functionally equivalent either way — not a blocker.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] Guard against division by zero in average and rate metric computations when there are no successful runs or when measured cost is zero.

finding_registry.description: The signals module imports ELIGIBLE_PHASES from theforge.task.prior_run_selector, violating the project convention to keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
